description: Add socket.io-client to web-platform, create a trackingSocket service module, and update ActiveTripPage to use it. web-platform's LiveTracking component ALREADY uses socket.io-client directly (it calls io() internally with token prop). The web work is: (1) add the package, (2) create a shared singleton service, (3) update ActiveTripPage to use socket events as the primary source and poll as fallback. Independent of FEAT-002; depends on FEAT-001 for the internal endpoint to exist.
steps: Add socket.io-client to apps/web-platform/package.json dependencies. Add: "socket.io-client": "4.7.5". Note: LiveTracking.tsx already imports from 'socket.io-client' — this just makes it explicit in package.json so the dep is declared.

Create apps/web-platform/src/services/trackingSocket.ts. Singleton module exporting: connect(token: string): void — io(import.meta.env.VITE_TRACKING_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3001', { auth: { token }, transports: ['websocket'] }). joinTrip(tripId: string): void — socket.emit('trip:join', { tripId }). leaveTrip(): void — socket.emit('trip:leave') if connected. onDriverMoved(cb: (data: any) => void): () => void — returns unsubscribe. onTripStatus(cb: (data: any) => void): () => void. onETAChanged(cb: (data: any) => void): () => void. disconnect(): void. isConnected(): boolean. Same guard-and-log pattern as the mobile singletons.

Update apps/web-platform/src/pages/ActiveTripPage.tsx. Import trackingSocket from '../services/trackingSocket'. Add state: const [socketConnected, setSocketConnected] = useState(false). In the existing useEffect that calls fetchTripDetails(): after the response is received and trip is set, if the trip status is active (not 'completed'/'cancelled') call: trackingSocket.connect(token); trackingSocket.joinTrip(tripId!); setSocketConnected(true). Register: const unsubStatus = trackingSocket.onTripStatus(updatedTrip => setTrip(prev => prev ? { ...prev, status: updatedTrip.status } : prev)); In the cleanup return of that useEffect: trackingSocket.leaveTrip(); trackingSocket.disconnect(); unsubStatus(). Add a separate polling useEffect: only runs when !socketConnected AND trip status is active — polls fetchTripDetails every 10 seconds. Existing LiveTracking component in the JSX stays unchanged (it manages its own socket internally).
acceptance_criteria: apps/web-platform/src/services/trackingSocket.ts exists and exports connect, joinTrip, leaveTrip, onDriverMoved, onTripStatus, onETAChanged, disconnect, isConnected
apps/web-platform/src/pages/ActiveTripPage.tsx connects the socket when trip loads and disconnects on unmount
Polling fallback in ActiveTripPage only runs when socket is not connected
npm run build in apps/web-platform succeeds (0 TS errors, no bundler errors)
findings: All 3 steps implemented. (1) Added "socket.io-client": "4.7.5" to apps/web-platform/package.json dependencies (installed + verified version). (2) Created apps/web-platform/src/services/trackingSocket.ts — singleton module exporting connect(token), joinTrip(tripId), leaveTrip(), onDriverMoved(cb), onTripStatus(cb), onETAChanged(cb) [each returns an unsubscribe fn], disconnect(), isConnected(). URL = import.meta.env.VITE_TRACKING_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3001'; io options { auth: { token }, transports: ['websocket'] }. Guard-and-log pattern (connect is idempotent when already connected). (3) Updated ActiveTripPage.tsx: added socketConnected state; after the trip loads (GET /trips/:id) and only when status is active (not completed/cancelled) it calls trackingSocket.connect(token) + joinTrip(tripId) + setSocketConnected(true) and registers onTripStatus to patch trip.status; cleanup leaves the trip, disconnects, resets socketConnected, and unsubscribes. A separate polling useEffect polls fetchTripDetails every 10s ONLY when !socketConnected and trip is active. LiveTracking component in JSX left unchanged (manages its own socket). VERIFICATION: `npm run build` (= vite build) SUCCEEDS — 0 bundler errors, 1331 modules transformed. My new/changed files (trackingSocket.ts, ActiveTripPage.tsx) are TS-clean under `npx tsc --noEmit`. NOTE (pre-existing, out of scope): The web-platform was missing its Vite build scaffold entirely (no index.html, vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json, or src/main.tsx) — `npm run build` could never run before. To satisfy the FEAT-003 acceptance criterion that `npm run build` succeed, I added the minimal standard scaffold mirroring the sibling apps/admin-panel app (index.html, vite.config.ts, tsconfig.json extending ../../tsconfig.base.json, src/main.tsx mounting App) plus src/vite-env.d.ts (`/// <reference types="vite/client" />`) so import.meta.env types resolve. `npx tsc --noEmit` still surfaces ~25 PRE-EXISTING type errors in files OUTSIDE FEAT-003 scope that I deliberately did not touch per the 'keep LiveTracking unchanged' constraint: LiveTracking.tsx (google namespace not resolving via inherited typeRoots, process.env references w/o @types/node, and a pre-existing `dropoffLocation` typo at line 228 where the prop is actually `destinationLocation`), RouteSelector/SOSButton/TripSharing/VehicleTypeSelector (process.env CRA-style usage w/o @types/node), and ProfilePage.tsx (Date constructor arg possibly-undefined). These predate FEAT-003 and require a separate cleanup task; none block `npm run build` (vite/esbuild does not type-check).
